title.bn: কমপ্লেক্সিটি ক্লাস P, NP আর NP-completeness

summary.en: Separate finding from checking, define decision classes, and follow the direction of polynomial reductions.
summary.bn: উত্তর খোঁজা আর যাচাই করা আলাদা করে বোঝো, decision class চেনো, আর reduction-এর দিক ঠিক রাখো।

notes: The demonstrated programs use C17; the lesson states their input and arithmetic bounds.

sections.title: Finding a certificate can be harder than checking it
Define the verifier before claiming NP
Hardness and membership are separate claims
What one fast solver would imply
Do not turn an open question into a slogan
Checkable does not yet mean efficiently findable

examples.title: Check a supplied colouring certificate
examples.explanationHtml: The C verifier accepts a three-colour assignment to a triangle. It checks colour ranges and every conflict edge. It demonstrates checking a witness, not a polynomial search for arbitrary three-colourings.

practice.title: Classify shortest-path existence with a nonnegative integer length bound K.
practice.statementHtml: Classify shortest-path existence with a nonnegative integer length bound K.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: The decision question asks whether some s-to-t path costs at most K. A polynomial shortest-path algorithm solves it, so it is in P and therefore NP. An explicit path is also a verifiable yes-certificate.

practice.title: State the two obligations for an NP-completeness proof of B.
practice.statementHtml: State the two obligations for an NP-completeness proof of B.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: First describe a polynomial-length certificate and a polynomial-time verifier for B. Then choose a known NP-complete A and give a polynomial-time transformation A to B preserving both yes and no instances.

practice.title: Explain why the O(nT) subset-sum DP does not establish that binary-encoded subset sum is in P.
practice.statementHtml: Explain why the O(nT) subset-sum DP does not establish that binary-encoded subset sum is in P.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: The target T occupies only about log2(T) bits. Its numeric value can be exponential in its representation length. A table indexed by every integer through T is therefore pseudo-polynomial, not polynomial in the binary input size.

practice.title: If A reduces to B and B has a polynomial algorithm, what follows?
practice.statementHtml: If A reduces to B and B has a polynomial algorithm, what follows?
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: Transform an A instance into a B instance in polynomial time, solve B in polynomial time, then return that answer. Thus A also has a polynomial algorithm. The implication does not run backwards from easy A to easy B.

quiz.prompt: What is the answer format of a decision problem?
quiz.explanation: Decision classes classify yes/no questions; search and optimisation are related but different tasks.
NP is defined through nondeterministic computation, equivalently polynomially verifiable yes-certificates.

options: P is a subset of NP
NP is a strict subset of P
Every NP-hard problem is in NP
quiz.explanation: A polynomial solver can be used by a polynomial verifier that ignores a certificate.

quiz.prompt: To prove B NP-hard from known NP-complete A, which reduction is needed?
options: A finite list of B examples
quiz.explanation: A solver for B must let us solve A after a polynomial transformation.

quiz.prompt: What else is required after proving B NP-hard to call it NP-complete?
options: A proof that B belongs to NP
quiz.explanation: NP-completeness combines hardness with a polynomial certificate verifier.

quiz.prompt: What would a polynomial algorithm for one NP-complete problem imply?
quiz.explanation: Every NP problem reduces to that complete problem, making every NP decision problem polynomial.

quiz.prompt: Why is O(nT) called pseudo-polynomial for binary subset sum?
options: It depends on numeric T rather than its bit length
It is always quadratic in bits
quiz.explanation: T may be exponentially larger than the number of bits used to encode it.

quiz.prompt: Which is an established NP-complete decision problem?
quiz.explanation: 3-SAT is NP-complete; the listed graph and search tasks have polynomial algorithms.

quiz.prompt: Can an NP-hard problem lie outside NP?
options: Yes, NP-hardness alone gives no verifier
quiz.explanation: An NP-hard problem need not be a polynomially verifiable decision problem.

quiz.prompt: What is known about whether P equals NP?
quiz.explanation: No proof currently settles equality; a slow implementation does not prove a problem inherently hard.

keyPoints.en: P contains decision problems with polynomial-time algorithms.
keyPoints.bn: polynomial সময়ে সমাধান করা যায় এমন decision সমস্যা P-তে থাকে।

keyPoints.en: NP contains decision problems with polynomially checkable certificates.
keyPoints.bn: polynomial সময়ে certificate যাচাই করা যায় এমন decision সমস্যা NP-তে থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Every problem in P also belongs to NP.
To prove B hard, reduce a known hard problem A to B.
keyPoints.bn: B কঠিন দেখাতে আগে থেকে কঠিন জানা A সমস্যাকে B-তে reduce করো।

keyPoints.en: NP-complete means both in NP and NP-hard.
keyPoints.bn: NP-complete হতে হলে NP-তে থাকতে হবে, আবার NP-hard-ও হতে হবে।

keyPoints.en: Pseudo-polynomial time may be exponential in the encoded input length.
keyPoints.bn: সংখ্যার মান ধরে polynomial সময় লাগলেও বিটের দৈর্ঘ্য ধরে exponential সময় লাগতে পারে।
